text: No jogo, Harbour City até abriu 2-0 com gols de Elias Okafor e Marek Barros, o craque do time que marcou e deu assistência [#905][#975]. Mas aos 43 minutos, o time perdeu Joon Whitfield expulso, o que complicou a partida [#870][#871]. Seabrook Town reagiu no segundo tempo, com ataques rápidos e cruzamentos, focando em contra-ataques após roubadas de bola. O time mandante criou chances, mas Seabrook foi ainda mais perigoso: seu xG, que mostra a qualidade das chances, foi 3.44, quase três vezes maior que o dos adversários, e marcou 4 gols no segundo tempo [#1104][#1448]. Nos minutos finais, Kian Romano brilhou marcando dois gols que viraram o placar, com chances muito boas (xG 0.605 e 0.952, ou seja, gols que ocorreriam quase 6 e 9 em 10 tentativas) [#1882][#1906]. Com esse ritmo forte e jogo envolvente, Seabrook Town levou a vitória e mostrou como pressão e contra-ataque são armas poderosas contra times que jogam com posse paciente, como Harbour City.

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in pt

- Seabrook Town won the match 4-2 despite being behind 2-0 early in the second half [#905, #975, #1104].
- Marek Barros scored a long-range goal with an xG of 0.009 and assisted the first Harbour City goal [#905, #975].
- Red card for Joon Whitfield at 43' weakened Harbour City [#871, #870].
- Seabrook Town's second half xG was 2.69 with 4 goals scored, showing strong offensive pressure [team_stats.second_half.Seabrook Town.xg, goals].
- Kian Romano scored two late goals in stoppage time with high xG values (0.605 and 0.952) to complete the comeback [#1882, #1906].

- Harbour City, playing a 4-2-3-1 with a patient short passing style, crafted their opening goal through a long, composed buildup of 17 passes over nearly a minute, culminating in a through ball assist from Marek Barros to Elias Okafor, who finished from 12.9 meters. This indicates their tactic of building from the back and waiting for openings rather than quick transitions [#905].

- Marek Barros' goal just after halftime resulted from a corner kick situation, exploiting set-piece opportunity and crossing into the box, consistent with Harbour City's formation which uses width and crossing options but relies mainly on patient build-up; here, a single long cross led directly to the goal, showing adaptability [#975].

- Seabrook Town, set up in a 3-4-3 formation focused on wide crossing play, relied heavily on regains and direct, aggressive attacking. Tariq Marlowe’s first goal came immediately after a ball recovery, with a quick shot from 10.4 meters without any build-up passes, illustrating Seabrook's punishing counter-attack threat and ability to capitalize on turnovers [#1104].

- Tactical adjustment by Seabrook Town around the 65th minute saw them increase pressing intensity (0.66 to 0.84) and directness (0.42 to 0.57), while raising their defensive line. This shift to a higher press and more direct play came during a chase scenario, leading to more box touches and big chances, exemplified by Callum Varga’s through ball goal from a regained ball, emphasizing Seabrook’s transition from possession to high-tempo attack [#1361, #1448].

- In late stages, Seabrook Town's goals by Kian Romano originated from quick counters and open play involving short through passes following regain, reflecting their exploit of Harbour City’s increased press and higher line after tactical changes by both sides to chase the game. This also highlights Seabrook's ability to penetrate a higher defensive line with rapid transition and width [#1882, #1906].

- The overall pattern reflects Harbour City's structured, possession-based patient build-up struggling against Seabrook's more dynamic 3-4-3 wide play and increased press/directness, leading to Harbour City having fewer meaningful chances despite early promise, while Seabrook Town leveraged turnover regains and set-piece variations to score four goals and capitalize on transitions [#team_styles, #team_stats].
